violations.why: Timer_C (prio 4) can preempt Timer_A between its read and write in the increment, so the write-back overwrites C's value (lost update).
Timer_C can preempt Timer_A between the read at 93 and the check at 95 and change timerCount, so the two reads see different values.
Timer_C can overwrite timerCount after Timer_A writes it and before Timer_A's check at 95, so the check doesn't see A's own value.
Timer_A (prio 3) preempts Timer_B (prio 2) between its write of 0 and its check, which makes the check see A's value instead of 0.
Timer_C (prio 4) preempts Timer_B between its write and its read and writes timerCount. Since C writes 0, the stored value doesn't change, but the interleaving is a write-write-read pattern.
Timer_Force (prio 3) preempts Timer_B between its write of 0 and its check and sets timerCount to 1, so the check at 108 fails.
